v.why: Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with the strongest op gives a larger gain than replacing an op that already carries signal.
Removing a strong direct edge costs much more than removing a weak one.
Giving node 1 its first input via a strong conv activates a whole branch, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Filling the empty edge into the output with a strong conv helps more than upgrading an existing op.
Adding an identity path where the slot is empty gives more benefit than swapping an already useful op.
Filling an empty slot with a useful conv adds a new path and so gains more than replacing an op that already contributes.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 is cut off from the output, so a stronger op on edge 2 has little effect.
With no input into node 1, edge 4 carries no signal, so upgrading it barely matters.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which is disconnected from the input when edge 0 is none, so the edit has almost no effect.
Adding a parametric-free path where the slot is empty gives a larger gain than replacing a useful op.
An identity shortcut to the output is worth much more when the slot was empty than when it replaces an existing op.
Replacing a strong conv with a weaker identity loses capacity, whereas replacing a weaker op does not.
Cutting a strong conv on the node-1 input edge hurts more than cutting a weak op.
Removing a useful conv edge hurts more than removing a weak op.
Deleting a strong conv costs more than deleting an op that contributes little.
Downgrading a strong conv to a pooling op loses more than replacing an op of similar weakness.
Pooling in an empty output edge adds a connected path, a gain absent when the slot already has an op.
Filling an empty edge into node 2 with the strongest conv adds more than upgrading an existing op.
Connecting node 1 to the input with a useful conv activates the node-1 branch, which beats modifying an existing op.
Without input to node 1, edge 2 passes nothing, so strengthening it has little effect.

Edge 2 only matters if edge 5 reaches the output, and edges 4 and 2 only matter if node 1 receives input from edge 0. I did not run anything to check these against benchmark data.
